description: We bring space data down to earth. We make tools that help farmers anywhere plan their land with confidence.
summary:
GrowÉire is a free website that helps farmers plan which crops to grow and in what order. Farmers know their land well, but the weather is changing and it's getting harder to know what to expect.

We use 25 years of NASA weather and satellite data to show how each month has usually gone on a farmer's land: how often it's been too dry, too wet, too hot or frosty. Everything is explained in plain, everyday language.

The farmer finds their field on a map and tells us what they've grown and what matters most to them. GrowÉire then compares their current rotation with two or three other options and explains the benefits, the risks and what's worth talking through with their advisor.

This answers the Field Shift challenge by combining NASA data with local soil, crops and the farmer's own priorities to find rotations that protect the soil and cope better with changing weather.

It matters because one bad season can cost a farm a whole year's income, and healthy soil takes years to rebuild. We started with Ireland, but it works anywhere, turning complex space data into simple advice for farmers.
details:
What it does: GrowÉire helps farmers choose which crops to grow and in what order. It shows how often each month has been too dry, too wet, too hot or frosty on their land, then compares their current rotation with two or three other options.

How it works: The farmer finds their field on a map, says what they've grown and what matters most to them. We use 25 years of NASA POWER weather and GPM rainfall data to count the bad months, and MODIS, SMAP and SRTM for extra detail. Each option explains why it was suggested, its benefits, its risks and what to ask an advisor.

Benefits: Clear, plain-language advice that farmers can check and take to their advisor.

Impact: Healthier soil and farms that cope better with changing weather. We started with Ireland, but it can work anywhere.

What makes it creative: It turns complex space data into simple counts anyone can understand, instead of a black-box score.

What we considered: Accessibility (large text, tap-only answers, plain words), cost (free, with no account or install), and trust (every number has a source, and the tool supports farmers rather than replacing them).

Tools: Vue and TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and NASA open data. Open source under the MIT licence.
